title: Technical Probe Design Lab and Onboard Sprint Canvas
abstract: Working canvas for designing short, role-specific technical probes plus a companion 30-day onboarding sprint for new hires. Goal: streamline hiring signal -> first 30 days impact by designing probes that map directly to early onboarding work and evidence collection.
purpose: Reduce false negatives/positives in technical interviews by aligning assessment tasks to predictable first-month work. Give hiring teams a repeatable lab for probe iteration and give managers a ready-to-run 30-day activation plan when offer is accepted.
audience: Hiring managers, interviewers (ICs), people ops recruiters, onboarding owners, eng leads who own role outcomes.
hiring_goals: Primary signals we need from probes: system design thinking, debugging methodology, tradeoff communication, and cultural fit through collaboration artifacts (PRs/discussion). Secondary signals: speed of ramp, code hygiene, basic infra literacy.
role_profile: Use this section to paste a 2-3 sentence operational profile for the role. Example: 'Backend infra engineer focused on inference runtime reliability: owns KV cache eviction strategies, latency instrumentation, and incident runbooks. First 30d outcome: implement and test a KV-cache eviction policy change with performance regression test.'
technical_probe_design_principles:
Guiding constraints (notes-to-self):
- Keep probe <= 90 minutes of candidate active time (can include 10-30 minutes of reading prep).
- Prefer tasks that produce an artifact (PR patch, short design doc, small reproducer test) we can put in repo-as-evidence.
- Avoid proprietary dataset or infra that candidates can't access; emulate with small fixtures.
- Make pass/fail and gradations explicit: what 'good' looks like and what minor gaps are acceptable.
- Include a short collaboration step: candidate reviews or comments on a tiny mock PR to observe feedback style and empathy.
- Document expected runtime environment and any helper scripts to reduce setup noise.
- Tag probe with primary signal mapping: {design, debugging, code-quality, infra, communication}.
probe_template_fields: (To copy into new probes) 1) Role profile link 2) Time budget 3) Inputs provided 4) Expected artifact(s) 5) Grading rubric (0-4 per signal) 6) Interviewer notes prompt 7) Post-probe followups (optional take-home) 8) Candidate experience checklist
interview_rubric_matrix:
Rubric quick grid (4pt scale):
- Design: 4=clear end-to-end plan with tradeoffs, 3=good plan missing minor considerations, 2=partial with major gaps, 1=fragmented, 0=no coherent plan.
- Implementation: 4=idiomatic, test-covered, handles edge cases, 3=good but missing tests or edge cases, 2=works but fragile, 1=broken, 0=no working output.
- Debugging/Reasoning: 4=structured hypotheses, reproducible steps, 3=solid rationale with small misses, 2=vague attempts, 1=flaky reasoning, 0=no attempt.
- Communication: 4=clear, concise, asks questions early, 3=adequate, 2=occasionally unclear, 1=poor, 0=non-collaborative.
- System/Infra Awareness: 4=knows cost/latency/ops implications, 3=aware of tradeoffs, 2=surface-level, 1=no ops sense, 0=anti-patterns.
Scoring guidance: >=16 strongly recommend, 12-15 consider context (culture fit, other signals), <12 need additional interview or decline.
grading_examples:
Examples for calibrators:
- Candidate A: built a small service, wrote unit tests, proposed a caching TTL vs size tradeoff with latency numbers -> Design 4, Impl 4, Debug 3, Comm 4, Infra 4 -> total 19 -> hire.
- Candidate B: solved algorithm but ignored infra constraints, wrote no tests -> Design 3, Impl 2, Debug 2, Comm 3, Infra 1 -> total 11 -> follow-up loop recommended.
- Candidate C: thoughtful but slow, lots of hand-wavy answers, good collaboration -> total 13 -> consider if team mentorship budget exists.
30_day_onboarding_sprint:
Sprint canvas for day 0-30 (copyable checklist):
Week 0 (pre-join): access + welcome doc, brief repo tour video, invite to buddy channel.
Days 1-3: env setup, small light-touch 'hello-world' patch to infra repo (mentor-reviewed), prioritized reading list.
Days 4-10: shadow existing owner on a bug triage rotation, own one small low-risk bug fix with test and perf note.
Days 11-20: implement a mini enhancement directly related to probe outcome (e.g., KV eviction policy tweak), submit PR and go through reviews.
Days 21-30: write short postmortem/lessons learned doc, present to team, identify next two sprint-level tickets.
Manager checkpoints: end of week 1 sync (blockers), end of week 2 demo, week 4 impact review + decision on pair-programming cadence.
Evidence collected for hiring loop: initial probe artifact + first PR + mentor review notes + week4 demo slides.
candidate_experience_checklist:
Checklist for recruiters and interviewers to ensure consistent candidate experience:
- Probe instructions sent 48h before with environment details.
- Clear time budget and deliverable expectations.
- Single contact person for logistics.
- Feedback timeline promised (usually 5 business days).
- Post-probe: short survey (2 questions) about clarity and fairness.
- If offer accepted: onboarding sprint doc + buddy assignment shared immediately.
decision_playbook:
How to convert probe results into hiring decisions (notes):
- Collate rubric scores and freeform interviewer notes.
- Check artifact lineage: is probe artifact substantial and self-authored?
- Apply weighting: design & implementation = 60%, communication & debugging = 30%, infra awareness = 10% (adjust for hard infra roles).
- If scores disagree by >5 points between interviewers, schedule a 30-min calibration conversation with hiring manager and senior interviewer.
- For borderline cases (12-15): run a focused follow-up (40min) on the single weakest signal rather than a full loop.
- Always document the rationale in the candidate record (JIRA/Hire log).
operational_notes: Practical ops: keep probe repo under /probes with one folder per role; each probe includes a docker-compose dev fixture for reproducibility. Label probes with 'time-budget' and 'primary-signal' tags. Rotate probes every 6 months to avoid stale artifacts. Add one new probe per quarter created by rotating engineer. Use post-hire evidence to retire probes that show poor predictive power.
open_questions:
Unresolved items we should decide:
- Standardized weighting per role family (infra vs app vs data)? (action: product council).
- Should recruiters ever screen out candidates based on probe artifact quality before full loop? (recruiting policy).
- Privacy/legal: what candidate artifacts do we retain long-term? (legal to advise).
- Can we measure probe predictive power quantitatively next 12 months? (analytics ticket).
next_steps: 1) Run a pilot with 3 upcoming infra hires in March. 2) Build an internal probe repo skeleton and CI-runner for basic sanity checks. 3) Schedule a 60-min calibration + rubric walkthrough with core interviewers. 4) Draft short candidate-facing probe FAQ.
notes_to_self: This doc purposefully mixes product-y crispness with sketchy ops notes — that's fine for now. When prototype proves out, migrate to Confluence and create templated Google Doc per role. Add a 'probe retirement' checkbox to end-to-end hiring retro.
